messages.content: Friday finally firmed up: RTP debrief 10-noon, lunch probably done 12:45. Before I ticket, can you refresh ORD-RDU round trips? I need Wednesday arrival with enough hotel/dinner margin, and I’d rather not get back to Chicago very late. United is fine if the timing still earns the fare.

Current best fits:
| itinerary | fare | Wed arrival | Fri return/trip | Friday buffer/trade-off |
| United nonstop | $318 | RDU 4:36 p.m. | 2:55-4:10 p.m.; nonstop | leave RTP about 12:50; ~95 min at RDU; best timing |
| American nonstop | $276 | RDU 3:55 p.m. | 5:25-6:49 p.m.; nonstop | easy buffer, later ORD arrival |
| Delta via ATL | $266 | RDU 4:48 p.m. | 3:20-7:08 p.m.; connection | cheapest, longest return |
United costs $42-$52 more but protects the after-lunch return without dragging the evening late.
How tight is 2:55 if lunch actually ends at 12:45? I won't check a bag, but I don't want to bolt out of the host's office.

With no checked bag, it is comfortable if you leave by about 12:55. RTP to RDU is usually 15-25 minutes then; call it airport arrival around 1:20. That leaves 90+ minutes. If lunch slips past 1:10, the later American return is safer, but for a 12:45 wrap I would keep United.
Reimbursement is fine up to $400. Is the cheaper itinerary worth it just for the $42?

Not really. The savings is small against getting home 2.5-3 hours later or adding a connection. The United pair also keeps Wednesday simple: 4:36 landing, rideshare to downtown Durham, hotel around 5:20, then 6:30 dinner.
Okay, use United. Aisle if free, no checked bag.

Use this for ticketing: United ORD-RDU Wed Nov. 4, 1:35-4:36 p.m.; United RDU-ORD Fri Nov. 6, 2:55-4:10 p.m.; fare about $318. Seat note: no-fee aisle if available, carry-on only. Local plan stays no car, downtown Durham hotel, and rideshare from RTP lunch around 12:50.

messages.content: Now that Raleigh-Durham is behind me, can you look at Madison for Dec. 12-13? Daniel and I will drive from Chicago, one night, Chazen exhibit Saturday afternoon and dinner with my daughter near State Street or the Capitol. I want flexible cancellation in case the weather looks bad, and I don't want parking to turn a good rate into a silly one.
Yes. One room for two adults. Do you want to stay central enough to park once, or is a short drive from a quieter area okay if the savings are real? Any all-in ceiling?

Park once is appealing, but I could be talked into west side if it saves enough. Try to keep it around $250 all-in with parking. One larger bed, and breakfast/coffee/fridge would be nice for a low-maintenance morning.

I found three workable refundable rates for Dec. 12-13:
| option | all-in est. incl. parking | location/logistics | breakfast + room basics | cancellation | trade-off |
| Hampton Inn & Suites Madison Downtown | ~$219 | near UW/State; walk to Chazen and most State St. dinners | breakfast included; coffee maker, mini-fridge listed | cancel by Dec. 11 evening | parking fee, but park once |
| Graduate Madison | ~$236 | closest to campus/State; very walkable | no free breakfast; coffee/fridge to verify | cancel by Dec. 11 | fun location, weaker morning setup |
| SpringHill Suites Madison/Hilldale | ~$162 | west side, easy/free parking; 12-15 min drive downtown | breakfast included; coffee/fridge listed | cancel by Dec. 11 | saves ~$55, but you move the car |
Can you sort the choice by total cost plus hassle, not just room rate?

Cost/hassle view: SpringHill is cheapest and easy to park, but you’ll drive to the museum and likely dinner. Hampton is about $57 more and has one parking bill, but then you can walk. Graduate costs more than Hampton once breakfast is excluded, so I would only pick it if you want the campus feel.
If dinner ends up on Williamson Street instead of State, does downtown still help?

Yes, but less dramatically. From Hampton or Graduate, Williamson Street is a short rideshare or an easy drive; from Hilldale you still drive to the Chazen first and then cross town for dinner. Downtown still reduces the number of parking decisions.
Double-check Hampton's amenities. Is it real breakfast and an in-room fridge, not just coffee in the lobby?

The Hampton listing shows hot breakfast included, in-room coffee maker, mini-fridge, and microwave for standard rooms. I’d still put coffee/fridge in the room notes, but it is not showing as lobby-only.
And the cancellation isn't prepaid?

Use the refundable Hampton rate, not the prepaid one. The cheaper prepaid rate saves about $15 and is not worth it for December driving. Refundable shows cancellation until Dec. 11 at 6 p.m.; confirm the exact timestamp on booking.
Then let's hold Hampton if it stays around that total. King would be great; queen is fine if that's the available refundable room.

Working recommendation: hold Hampton Inn & Suites Madison Downtown, Dec. 12-13, 1 room/2 adults, refundable, estimated $219 all-in with parking and tax. Request king; queen acceptable if that is the refundable room. Notes: quiet room, in-room coffee maker and mini-fridge, breakfast included, and parking instructions. Trade-off: about $55 more than Hilldale, but better for winter convenience because you can park once and walk to Chazen/State Street, with Williamson Street still a short rideshare if plans shift.
